    The Lizzie Borden cast Netflix lineup is now confirmed, with Ella Beatty leading Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story as Lizzie Borden. The fourth installment of Netflix’s Monster anthology premiered on September 17, 2026, with eight episodes available to stream in the United States. The cast also includes Charlie Hunnam, Vicky Krieps, Rebecca Hall, Billie Lourd, Jessica Barden, Joey Pollari and Sarah Paulson.

    Death & Tragedy

    The new season brings one of America’s most recognizable criminal cases to Netflix through a scripted period drama. Beatty plays Lizzie, while the surrounding cast portrays members of her family, people connected to the Borden household and figures tied to the story’s later legacy.

    Netflix lists the series as a TV-MA drama with eight episodes. The episodes range from 39 minutes to just over an hour, giving the season room to cover the Borden household, the killings, the investigation and the trial.

      • Movie & TV Streaming

    Ella Beatty plays Lizzie Borden

    Ella Beatty has the central role in Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story.

    She portrays Lizzie Borden, the Massachusetts woman accused of killing her father and stepmother in 1892. Beatty’s character remains at the heart of the season from its opening episode through the courtroom story.

    Netflix describes its version of Lizzie as a young woman trapped inside a restrictive Victorian household. Her relationship with her father, stepmother and the household staff forms a major part of the drama.

    Beatty is a relatively new screen performer compared with several of her co-stars. Her previous credits include Feud: Capote vs. The Swans and If I Had Legs I’d Kick You. She has also appeared on Broadway in Appropriate.

    The Netflix role marks a major leading opportunity for Beatty. She carries a story that requires the character to move through family conflict, violence, public scrutiny and a highly publicized trial.

    Netflix’s official material describes the season as its first Monster installment centered on a female subject. That places Beatty at the center of the anthology’s latest chapter.

    Movies

    Charlie Hunnam plays Andrew Borden

    Charlie Hunnam portrays Andrew Borden, Lizzie’s father.

    Andrew is one of the central figures in the Borden household. The series depicts him as a wealthy and controlling father whose relationship with his daughters contributes to the tension inside the family.

    Hunnam is already familiar to Monster viewers. He previously appeared as Ed Gein in Monster: The Ed Gein Story, the third season of the anthology.

    His return gives the franchise a recognizable connection between its third and fourth installments.

    Hunnam became widely known through Sons of Anarchy, where he played Jax Teller. His film credits include Pacific Rim and The Gentlemen.

    In the new season, his role is dramatically different from his previous Monster character. Instead of portraying the central criminal subject, Hunnam plays a member of Lizzie’s family whose death becomes the center of the case.

    TV Shows & Programs

    Rebecca Hall plays Abby Borden

    Rebecca Hall takes the role of Abby Borden, Lizzie’s stepmother.

    Abby is another key member of the Borden household. Her relationship with Lizzie becomes an important part of the series, particularly as the story examines the family’s strained domestic environment.

    Hall has built an extensive film career through projects such as The Prestige, The Town, Christine and Passing. She brings that experience to a period role that requires her to portray a complicated family relationship.

    Abby Borden’s importance to the story goes beyond her position as Lizzie’s stepmother. She is also one of the two people whose deaths led to Lizzie’s historic trial.

    Netflix identifies Hall among the principal stars alongside Beatty, Krieps and Hunnam.

    Her performance helps establish the family circumstances that dominate the early episodes before the investigation becomes the primary focus.

    Vicky Krieps plays Bridget “Maggie” Sullivan

    Vicky Krieps plays Bridget “Maggie” Sullivan, the Borden family’s live-in maid.

    Death & Tragedy

    Maggie has a particularly important relationship with Lizzie in the Netflix production. The character works inside the Borden household and becomes closely connected with Lizzie as the story develops.

    Netflix describes the two women as being trapped in a household marked by humiliation and cruelty. Their relationship becomes one of the season’s main dramatic threads.

    Krieps has previously appeared in Phantom Thread and Monster: The Ed Gein Story. Her return to the anthology makes her another performer appearing in consecutive seasons.

    The role also gives Krieps a strong presence outside the immediate Borden family. Maggie sees the household from the perspective of an employee rather than a family member.

    That position allows the character to interact with Lizzie differently from Andrew, Abby and Emma.

    Billie Lourd plays Emma Borden

    Billie Lourd portrays Emma Borden, Lizzie’s older sister.

    Emma is one of the few people who shares Lizzie’s family history from childhood. Her presence gives the series an important sibling dynamic.

    Movie & TV Streaming

    The relationship between the sisters is central to the story because Emma remains connected to Lizzie during the period surrounding the murders and trial.

    Lourd is known for American Horror Story, Scream Queens and her appearances in the Star Wars sequel trilogy. Her film credits also include Booksmart and The Last Showgirl.

    Netflix identifies Emma as Lizzie’s older sister. The character provides another perspective on the family and helps broaden the story beyond the relationship between Lizzie and her parents.

    Lourd’s casting also adds another established performer to a season led by Beatty.

    Jessica Barden plays Nance O’Neil

    Jessica Barden appears as Nance O’Neil, an actress who becomes connected to Lizzie.

    Unlike Andrew, Abby and Emma, Nance does not belong to the Borden household. Her connection to Lizzie comes through the world outside the family.

    The character becomes part of Lizzie’s life after the trial period and is associated with the wider public story surrounding her.

    Movies

    Barden is best known to many viewers for The End of the F**ing World*. She has also appeared in Hanna, The Lobster and Dune: Prophecy.

    Her character helps the series explore what happens to Lizzie after the most closely watched part of her case has passed.

    That gives Barden a role that differs from the performers playing members of Lizzie’s immediate family.

    Joey Pollari plays John Morse

    Joey Pollari portrays John Morse, Lizzie’s maternal uncle.

    John Morse adds another family connection to the story. His presence becomes relevant to the investigation surrounding the Borden household.

    Netflix’s cast material lists Pollari among the principal performers, while current cast information identifies Morse as Lizzie’s uncle.

    Pollari has appeared in projects including American Crime and Love, Simon. His role in the Netflix series places him inside the historical family story rather than among the modern-day performers surrounding it.

    Morse’s character gives the season another person connected to Lizzie by family ties, widening the circle around the central case.

    TV Shows & Programs

    Sarah Paulson plays Aileen Wuornos

    Sarah Paulson has one of the season’s most unusual roles.

    She portrays Aileen Wuornos, the notorious American criminal whose story belongs to a much later period than Lizzie Borden’s.

    Wuornos was not involved in the 1892 Borden murders. Instead, Netflix uses her character as part of the season’s exploration of Lizzie Borden’s continuing influence.

    Netflix’s Tudum explains that Wuornos appears in scenes set decades after the original Borden story. Her character becomes fascinated by Lizzie and her legacy.

    Paulson is a longtime collaborator of Ryan Murphy. Her credits include American Horror Story, Ratched, Bird Box and American Crime Story.

    Her casting creates a connection between two very different chapters of American true-crime history.

    It also gives Paulson another role within Murphy’s television universe.

    The main cast at a glance

    Netflix’s official cast listing confirms Beatty, Krieps, Hunnam, Hall, Barden, Pollari, Lourd and Paulson as the principal cast.

    Movie & TV Streaming

    The cast brings together new and returning faces

    One notable feature of the season is the combination of actors new to the Monster anthology and performers returning from previous installments.

    Beatty is new to the franchise and leads the season. Hunnam and Krieps, meanwhile, previously appeared in Monster: The Ed Gein Story.

    That continuity gives the anthology a familiar element while allowing each performer to take on a new character.

    The fourth season also brings together actors with different backgrounds. Beatty has substantial theater experience, while Hunnam is known for both television and film. Hall has worked extensively in dramatic cinema, and Paulson has become one of Ryan Murphy’s most frequent collaborators.

    The result is an ensemble built around a historical central character but supported by performers from several generations of screen and stage work.

    What the Netflix season covers

    The story begins inside the Borden household and gradually moves toward the murders, investigation and trial.

    Movies

    Netflix’s episode listings show the progression across all eight installments.

    The opening episode, Bloodbath, introduces Lizzie and Maggie. Later episodes move deeper into the family conflict before the story reaches the murders and their aftermath.

    The seventh episode, The Trial of the Century, focuses directly on the courtroom proceedings. The eighth episode, Carnival, deals with the burden of Lizzie’s legacy.

    This structure means the cast remains important throughout the entire season rather than serving only as a setup for the murder investigation.

    Beatty’s Lizzie stays at the center, while the supporting performances establish the relationships that drive the narrative.

    The series is now streaming on Netflix

    Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story premiered on Netflix on September 17, 2026.

    The complete season contains eight episodes, allowing U.S. viewers to watch the story through to its conclusion rather than waiting for weekly installments. Netflix lists the series as TV-MA and categorizes it as a drama, period piece and crime production.

    Reference

    For viewers searching for the current Lizzie Borden cast Netflix lineup, the central answer is Ella Beatty as Lizzie Borden, supported by a major ensemble that includes Charlie Hunnam, Rebecca Hall, Vicky Krieps, Billie Lourd, Jessica Barden, Joey Pollari and Sarah Paulson.

    The cast gives the new season a mix of historical characters, family members and later figures connected to Lizzie’s enduring place in American true-crime culture.

    Why the cast is central to the new season

    The success of the story depends heavily on the relationships between its characters.

    Beatty must carry Lizzie’s transformation through the season. Hunnam and Hall establish the difficult family environment surrounding her, while Lourd provides the sibling relationship that remains important to the story.

    Krieps brings a different perspective through Maggie, who works inside the household but is not part of the Borden family.

    Barden and Pollari broaden the circle of people surrounding Lizzie, while Paulson’s appearance connects the story to a later chapter in the history of American crime.

    Death & Tragedy

    With all eight episodes now available, viewers can see how these performances fit together across the full season.
